item.title: ACLU of Indiana sues Ball State over protest rules
item.description: The plaintiffs are students who have protested against Ball State, mainly asking it to divest from any financial ties to Israel. The ACLU says university policies violated their First and Fourteenth Amendment rights.

item.title: Gov. Mike Braun gives himself 'B+' on 2026 session, calls Trump's Iran action 'long overdue'
item.description: Indiana Gov. Mike Braun is giving this year’s legislative session a “B+,” saying 51 of his 58 priority bills passed.

item.title: Bill that changes selection process for Marion County judges creates tension between lawmakers
item.description: A bill changing how Marion County Superior Court judges are selected is creating tension between Indianapolis lawmakers.

item.title: AES Indiana cancels first Indianapolis community open house due to threats
item.description: The utility company created the event as an opportunity for customers to connect with staff and ask questions.

item.title: Marion County detained over 1,000 immigrants for ICE last year
item.description: A WFYI data analysis of Marion County Jail records reveals that more than 1,000 people from at least 55 countries were held on immigration detainers in 2025.

item.title: Former Indianapolis Mayor Greg Ballard runs as independent in secretary of state race
item.description: Former Indianapolis Mayor Greg Ballard will join the increasingly crowded race for Indiana Secretary of State.

item.title: A new visual record of Indianapolis' past is emerging from crime scene photos
item.description: Originally taken to document acts of violence, crime scene photos now serve as a vital window into a world that no longer exists.

item.title: A-F grades for schools are back. Indiana approves accountability model
item.description: Indiana education leaders approved a new A-to-F school accountability grading system Wednesday, restarting a process that has been paused since 2021.

item.title: How Indianapolis' new road safety team intends to eliminate traffic deaths by 2035
item.description: Indianapolis officials started work on a decade-long project meant to make streets safer for bikers, pedestrians and drivers.

item.title: State treasurer warns AES-BlackRock deal won't prioritize Indiana residents
item.description: The Indiana state treasurer is calling on federal regulators to review of the new acquisition deal announced to sell Indianapolis’s electric utility company to out-of-state investors.
